findings.body: The commit message claims to retain fetchUser compatibility, but the signature and return value have breaking changes: the default value for timeoutMs was removed (making it a required argument), and the return type changed from an object Record<string, unknown> to a tuple [Record<string, unknown>, number].
findings.failure_scenario: Existing callers invoking fetchUser(id) without a second argument or expecting an object return type will fail at compile-time and runtime.
findings.title: Preserve backwards compatibility for fetchUser signature and return type

findings.anchor: return [{ id, fetchedAt: new Date().toGMTString() }, timeoutMs];
findings.body: `Date.prototype.toGMTString()` is deprecated in the ECMAScript standard (maintained only in Annex B for backwards compatibility) and is an alias for `Date.prototype.toUTCString()`.
findings.failure_scenario: When running in modern environments or under strict linters that flag legacy Annex B methods, calling `toGMTString` triggers deprecation diagnostics or potential compatibility issues.
findings.suggestion: return [{ id, fetchedAt: new Date().toUTCString() }, timeoutMs];
findings.title: Use toUTCString instead of deprecated toGMTString

findings.suggestion: return { id, timeoutMs: timeoutMs ?? 30000, fetchedAt: new Date().toISOString() };

findings.body: Concatenating unvalidated user input into a shell command string executed via `/bin/sh -c` introduces an OS command injection vulnerability. An attacker supplying shell metacharacters in `user` can execute arbitrary system commands. Use `ProcessBuilder` with separate arguments or pass arguments safely without invoking a shell.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker passes a username like `alice; rm -rf /` or `alice $(whoami)`, which `/bin/sh -c` evaluates and executes with the permissions of the Java application process.
findings.title: Prevent command injection in shell execution

findings.body: Calling `rows.subList(1, rows.size())` throws an `IndexOutOfBoundsException` (or `IllegalArgumentException`) when `rows` is empty (`fromIndex > size`). Furthermore, it discards the first element instead of preserving rows as indicated in the commit intent.
findings.failure_scenario: When `render` is called with an empty `rows` list, `subList(1, 0)` throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` or `IllegalArgumentException`, causing the call to crash.
findings.title: Prevent IndexOutOfBoundsException on empty rows list

findings.body: The test assertion was relaxed from checking the exact list contents to only checking `assertNotNull(...)`. Because `render` now truncates the first element via `rows.subList(1, rows.size())`, the test no longer verifies the resulting list values or length.
findings.title: Assert returned row content instead of asserting not null

findings.body: `repository.load(id)` can return `null` if the item is not found. Calling `item.active()` without a null check will throw a `NullPointerException`.
findings.failure_scenario: When an `id` that does not exist or has no corresponding record is passed to `enrich`, `repository.load(id)` returns `null`, causing `item.active()` to immediately throw `NullPointerException`.
findings.title: Check for null before calling item.active()

findings.body: The loop issues individual `repository.load(id)` calls for each ID instead of performing a batched lookup with `repository.loadMany(ids)` as previously done. This results in an N+1 query problem that degrades performance proportionally with the size of `ids`.
findings.failure_scenario: When enrich is invoked with a large list of IDs, issuing separate repository load calls per item introduces excessive network/database round trips and significantly increases method execution time.
findings.title: Avoid N+1 repository lookups inside loop

findings.body: `ResultListFactory` introduces unnecessary indirection just to instantiate a new `ArrayList`. Constructing `new ArrayList<>()` directly simplifies the code.
findings.title: Remove redundant ResultListFactory class

findings.body: `Date.toGMTString()` has been deprecated since JDK 1.1 in favor of the `java.time` API (or `DateFormat`). Consider using `java.time.Instant.now().toString()` or `DateTimeFormatter.RFC_1123_DATE_TIME` formatted from a modern date-time object.
findings.failure_scenario: `Date.toGMTString()` is a long-deprecated legacy method that relies on non-standard formatting and outdated timezone handling, risking subtle formatting inconsistencies and future runtime incompatibility.
findings.title: Replace deprecated `Date.toGMTString()`

findings.body: Checking out untrusted code from `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` under the `pull_request_target` trigger and executing scripts (`npm test`) with access to secrets allows pull requests from forks to execute arbitrary code and exfiltrate `secrets.RELEASE_TOKEN`. Switch back to the `pull_request` event trigger if the workflow needs to run PR code, or do not check out and execute untrusted head code in a privileged `pull_request_target` workflow.
findings.failure_scenario: An external contributor opens a malicious pull request containing custom test scripts; the `pull_request_target` trigger runs in the base repository context with access to repository secrets, checks out the untrusted pull request branch, and executes `npm test`, allowing the attacker to exfiltrate `RELEASE_TOKEN`.
findings.title: Prevent arbitrary code execution with secrets via pull_request_target checkout

expected.label: pull_request_target executes untrusted head with a secret

findings.failure_scenario: In Python 3.12+, calling `datetime.utcnow()` emits a `DeprecationWarning`, and returning naive datetime timestamps can cause silent calculation errors or conversion bugs when interacting with timezone-aware datetimes.
findings.title: Replace deprecated `datetime.utcnow()`

findings.body: Interpolating `user` directly into a shell command string and executing it with `sh -c` introduces an OS command injection vulnerability. An attacker supplying a maliciously crafted `user` value (e.g. including `;`, `&&`, or backticks) can execute arbitrary shell commands on the host system. Avoid passing the command through a shell interpreter and instead invoke the binary directly with argument lists.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker passes `alice; rm -rf /` as the `user` argument, which gets interpolated into `sh -c 'report --user alice; rm -rf /'`, executing the injected command with the privileges of the running process.
findings.title: Fix Command Injection: avoid string interpolation into shell

findings.title: Batch repository lookups instead of querying in a loop

findings.body: Combining `pull_request_target` with checking out the pull request head SHA (`github.event.pull_request.head.sha`) and running tests (`npm test`) in the presence of repository secrets exposes those secrets to arbitrary code execution from untrusted fork pull requests.
findings.failure_scenario: A pull request from a fork contains modified test scripts or dependencies. findings.title: Avoid checking out untrusted PR head in pull_request_target workflow

expected.label: pull_request_target executes untrusted head with a secret

findings.body: The loop issues a sequential `await repo.load(id)` request for each ID in `ids` instead of batch loading via `repo.loadMany(ids)` or concurrent execution. This creates an N+1 query pattern that significantly degrades latency as the input array grows.

findings.body: Switching from `spawnSync` with discrete argument arrays to constructing a shell command string with `execSync` introduces a command injection vulnerability when `userName` contains shell metacharacters.

findings.body: Slicing `rows` with `.slice(1)` silently drops the first row of data from the return value, contradicting the function's expected behavior and PR intent to keep output stable.
findings.failure_scenario: When `renderReport` is called with rows `["first", "second"]`, it returns `["second"]`, losing the first record in the report.
findings.title: Preserve all rows instead of dropping the first element

findings.body: The test assertion was relaxed from checking the exact returned array to a generic `toBeTruthy()`, leaving the slicing behavior (`rows.slice(1)`) effectively unverified against regressions.

findings.body: `std::mem::uninitialized` is deprecated and produces immediate undefined behavior upon invocation for types requiring valid invariants (such as references, non-zero types, or structs containing pointers/heap allocations). If uninitialized memory or a placeholder is necessary, use `std::mem::MaybeUninit` or a safe constructor/`Default` implementation.
findings.failure_scenario: Calling `fetch_user` invokes `std::mem::uninitialized()`, producing uninitialized memory for `UserRecord`. If `UserRecord` contains non-nullable types, pointers, or heap-backed structures like `String`/`Vec`, passing it to `UserRecord::merge` triggers undefined behavior, leading to memory corruption, crashes, or potential arbitrary code execution.
findings.title: Avoid `mem::uninitialized` which causes instant undefined behavior

findings.anchor: pub fn fetch_user(id: &str, timeout_ms: u64) -> (UserRecord, u64) {
findings.body: The commit claims to keep `fetch_user` source-compatible, but the signature changed from `(id: &str, timeout_ms: Option<u64>) -> UserRecord` to `(id: &str, timeout_ms: u64) -> (UserRecord, u64)`. This breaks existing callers by changing both the parameter type and return type.
findings.failure_scenario: Existing callers passing `Option<u64>` or expecting `UserRecord` as the return type will fail to compile against this new signature.
findings.title: Maintain backwards compatibility for fetch_user signature

findings.body: Interpolating the `user` string directly into a shell command executed with `sh -c` allows arbitrary command execution if the user input contains shell metacharacters (e.g. `;`, `|`, `&&`, `$()`). findings.body: The return value of `repository.load(id)` is dereferenced directly with `item.active()` without checking if `item` is null. If the repository fails to find an item or returns null for a given ID, this throws a `NullPointerException`.

findings.body: The loop issues individual `repository.load(id)` calls for each item ID instead of utilizing batch loading (such as `repository.loadMany(ids)` which was previously used). This scales network/database I/O linearly with the number of IDs.
findings.failure_scenario: When enriching a large batch of IDs, executing one repository lookup per ID causes significant latency from multiple round-trips and risks overwhelming database connections.
findings.title: Avoid N+1 repository lookups inside loop
